root_cause: When a focused element is removed from the DOM, the focus trap's mutation observer attempts to restore focus to the initial focus node. However, if the removed element had tabindex=0 and there are no elements with positive tabindex in the trap, the focus-in handler incorrectly tries to refocus the detached element before falling back to the initial focus node. Since the detached element is no longer connected, focusing it fails silently, leaving focus on the body.
repair_strategy: Modify the focus-in handler in index.js to check if the most recently focused node is still connected and focusable before attempting to refocus it. If not, immediately fall back to the initial focus node.
expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will remain trapped within the basket dialog after removing an item, ensuring keyboard users can continue interacting with the dialog without escaping to the page background.
functional_risks: The isConnected property may not be available in very old browsers, but the focus-trap already assumes modern DOM APIs.
Checking isFocusable adds minimal overhead only in the rare case of focus escape.
Preserves all existing behavior for non-detached MRU nodes.
verification_requirements: After removing the first basket item via Enter key, focus must remain on the close button or another item in the basket.
Tab navigation must cycle correctly within the basket after item removal.
Closing and reopening the basket must restore initial focus to the close button.
